findings.claim: Existing columns are treated as satisfied by name only, so type/nullability drift can produce a false noop instead of a refusal or repair plan.
findings.evidence: Acceptance requires diff vs `live` and `noop` only when satisfied; `emit_table_diff` checks only `existing.columns.iter().any(|c| c.name == col.name)` and immediately `continue`s, ignoring `TableMeta`'s `sql_type` and `nullable` fields.
findings.suggested_fix: When a matching live column exists, compare its SQL type and nullability against the requested `ColumnSpec`; return a non-additive drift error if they differ.

findings.claim: Caller-declared indexes on existing tables are always re-emitted, so an already-existing caller index cannot diff to no-op as required.
findings.evidence: Acceptance criterion: "A caller index that already exists diffs to no-op." The implementation states `TableMeta` lacks index introspection and unconditionally loops `for idx in &table.indexes { emit_index(...) }`, making `statements` non-empty and `noop` false for any spec index on an existing table.
findings.suggested_fix: Extend the live metadata input to include indexes or remove the no-op requirement from the contract; then suppress emission and mark `exists: true` when an index is already present.

findings.claim: Validation allows a caller index to use the same name as the generated tenant index, causing the caller's requested index to be silently skipped by `IF NOT EXISTS`.
findings.evidence: `validate_table` only checks duplicates among caller-provided `idx.name` values, while `emit_tenant_block` in `crates/fdb-app/src/provision/ddl.rs` generates an implicit index named `format!("{t}_tenant_idx")`; a caller index with that name but different columns will be emitted after the generated tenant index and no-op because the name already exists.
findings.suggested_fix: For tenant-scoped tables, reject any caller `IndexSpec.name` equal to the reserved generated tenant index name, or choose a generated name that cannot collide and validate that reservation.
